        1. clone the repo git@github.com:zelarhq/nodejs-welcome.git
        2. analyse the contents of the repo and create following.

function.name: create_a_docker_file
function.description: This function generates a Dockerfile in the specified directory with basic configuration. The Dockerfile will be tailored to a simple Python application. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

directory_name.description: The name of the directory where the Dockerfile will be created. It should be a valid directory path relative to the current working directory.

base_image.description: The base image to use for the Dockerfile, representing the starting point for the build.

maintainer.description: The name of the maintainer or author of the Dockerfile.

expose_port.description: The port number that the container should expose. This is typically the port that the application listens on.

entrypoint.description: The command that will be executed when the Docker container starts.

function.name: create_kubernetes_yaml_file
function.description: Generates a Kubernetes deployment and service YAML file in the specified repository directory. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

directory_name.description: The name of the directory where the Kubernetes YAML file will be created. This should be the root directory of the repository.

deployment_name.description: The name of the deployment to be created. This should be a unique identifier for the deployment.

image_name.description: The name of the Docker image to be used in the deployment. Include the image version tag if necessary.

replicas.description: The number of replicated pods desired in the deployment.

port.description: The port number that the container exposes for communication.

service_type.description: The type of Kubernetes service to be created for the deployment.

message.content:
Below is a complete, ready‑to‑use set of files that will get your **nodejs‑welcome** repository containerised, exposed in Kubernetes, and automatically built on every push to `main`.  
I’ve kept the instructions generic so you can drop them into the repo and then commit/push yourself.

---

## 1️⃣  Dockerfile (Node.js)

```dockerfile
# Dockerfile
# ------------------------------------
# Base image – use the official Node 18 slim image
FROM node:18-alpine

# Working directory inside the container
WORKDIR /app

# Copy package files first to leverage Docker cache
COPY package*.json ./

# Install production dependencies only
RUN npm ci --only=production

# Copy the rest of the source code
COPY . .

# Expose the port your app listens on
EXPOSE 3000

# Default command
CMD ["node", "app.js"]
```

> **Why this Dockerfile?**  
> * `node:18-alpine` is small, secure, and contains everything you need to run a Node app.  
> * `npm ci` guarantees a clean install that matches `package-lock.json`.  
> * The container listens on port **3000** – the default for most Express apps (adjust if your app uses a different port).

---

## 2️⃣  Kubernetes manifests

Create a folder called `k8s/` (or any name you prefer) and add the following two files.

### 2.1  `k8s/deployment.yaml`

```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: nodejs-welcome-deployment
  labels:
    app: nodejs-welcome
spec:
  replicas: 2
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: nodejs-welcome
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: nodejs-welcome
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: nodejs-welcome
        image: <YOUR_REGISTRY>/nodejs-welcome:latest   # <-- replace with your registry
        ports:
        - containerPort: 3000
        env:
        - name: NODE_ENV
          value: production
```

### 2.2  `k8s/service.yaml`

```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: nodejs-welcome-service
spec:
  type: ClusterIP
  selector:
    app: nodejs-welcome
  ports:
  - protocol: TCP
    port: 80          # Service port exposed inside the cluster
    targetPort: 3000  # Container port
```

> **Tip:**  
> Replace `<YOUR_REGISTRY>` with the registry you’ll push to (e.g. `ghcr.io/zelarhq/nodejs-welcome`).  
> If you want external access, change `type: ClusterIP` to `NodePort` or `LoadBalancer` and adjust the `port` accordingly.

---

## 3️⃣  GitHub Actions workflow

Create the directory `.github/workflows/` (if it doesn’t exist) and add the following file:

### `.github/workflows/docker-build.yml`

```yaml
name: Build & Push Docker Image

on:
  push:
    branches:
      - main

jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

    steps:
      # Checkout the repo
      - uses: actions/checkout@v3

      # Set up Docker Buildx (multi‑arch support)
      - name: Set up Docker Buildx
        uses: docker/setup-buildx-action@v2

      # Log in to Docker Hub (or any registry you use)
      - name: Login to Docker Hub
        uses: docker/login-action@v2
        with:
          username: ${{ secrets.DOCKERHUB_USERNAME }}
          password: ${{ secrets.DOCKERHUB_TOKEN }}

      # Build the image and push it
      - name: Build & Push
        uses: docker/build-push-action@v4
        with:
          context: .
          push: true
          tags: ${{ secrets.DOCKERHUB_USERNAME }}/nodejs-welcome:latest
```

> **What you need to do:**
> 1. Create two repository secrets in GitHub:
>    * `DOCKERHUB_USERNAME` – your Docker Hub (or other registry) username  
>    * `DOCKERHUB_TOKEN` – a Docker Hub personal access token with **write** permissions
> 2. If you’re using GitHub Container Registry (GHCR) or another registry, adjust the `tags` line and the login step accordingly.

---

## 4️⃣  Commit & Push

Open a terminal, navigate to the root of the cloned repo, and run:

```bash
# Add the new/updated files
git add Dockerfile k8s/*.yaml .github/workflows/docker-build.yml

# Commit with a clear message
git commit -m "Add Dockerfile, Kubernetes manifests, and CI workflow"

# Push to the main branch
git push origin main
```

> **After pushing**  
> GitHub Actions will automatically trigger the workflow, build the Docker image, and push it to your registry.  
> Once the image is available, you can deploy it to any Kubernetes cluster using:

```bash
kubectl apply -f k8s/
```

---

### Quick sanity check

1. **Docker image**  
   ```bash
   docker pull <YOUR_REGISTRY>/nodejs-welcome:latest
   docker run -p 3000:3000 <YOUR_REGISTRY>/nodejs-welcome:latest
   ```
   Visit `http://localhost:3000` to confirm the app is running.

2. **Kubernetes**  
   ```bash
   kubectl get pods
   kubectl get svc
   ```

If everything looks good, you’re all set! 🎉

Feel free to tweak the replica count, environment variables, or service type to match your production needs.
